title: Publishers Of Krivoe Zerkalo Will Suspend Publication For Two Months

page_data.en:
(Headquarters) Office Notes

Deputy Commissioner in Charge.

Date: August 11, 1937.
S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 8012
Date 11- 8- 37

Forwarded herewith is a circular in Russian,
together with translation, dated August 7, which has
been received from the "Krivoe Zerkalo". It states
that the magazine will suspend publication for two
months and that the next issue will appear on October 2,
1937.

In view of the fact that the Chinese Authorities
are very busy in consequence of the present/political
situation and that most of their archives and documents
have been shifted and stored away at places of safety,
they are as yet unable to give a reply as to whether
this publication is registered or not. In the meantime
D.S. Tcheremshansky will be instructed to call on the
editor to ascertain from him whether his paper has been
properly registered or not.

copy of translation sent to M'Early.

D.B. Ross
P.A. to D.C. (Sp.Br.)

"KRIVOYE ZERKALO"
1025/25 Bubbling Well Rd.
A Weekly Publication of Free Laughter.

Shanghai, Saturday,
August 7, 1937.

Dear Reader!

With deep sorrow and weeping for the dead, I have
to inform you that the publishers of "Krivoe Zerkalo"
at an extraordinary meeting, held a few days ago, unanimously
decided to call a halt to its mad activities for a period
of two months.

A whole series of tragic circumstances have compelled
us to take this decision; amongst these a certain place
may be alloted to the hunt, instituted against us by certain
Russian members of the French Police(?), who are vehemently
pro-Japanese and Fascisti. But their "blows" as a matter
of fact are just bites of mad drones......

The next - IIth issue of the "Krivoye Zerkalo" will
appear on Saturday, October 2, 1937 and from that date
onwards will be published regularly.

The subscription, paid for August and September
months will be automatically transferred to October and
November. Those who have failed to pay for the past months,
it is to be hoped, upbraided by their conscience, will
pay their dues.

Do not weep so bitterly, dear Reader! We are parting
only for a couple of months, which will pass like meteors.
We do not wish to deprive you of the hope that we may
renew our activities even before the period stated - quite
suddenly.

Meanwhile, goodbye until we meet again soon!
Here's a good shake of the paw!

Ed. Tiapkin-Liapkin, Representative of the
entire Brotherhood of Krivoe Zerkalo

自由欢笑周刊。

上海，星期六，
1937年8月7日。

亲爱的读者！

怀着深深的悲痛和对死者的哀哭，我不得不通知您，《Krivoe Zerkalo》的出版商在几天前召开的一次特别会议上，一致决定将其疯狂的活动暂停两个月。

一系列悲剧性的情况迫使我们做出这一决定；其中，某些亲日且信奉法西斯主义的法国警察中的俄罗斯成员对我们发起的追捕，也占有一席之地。但事实上，他们的“打击”不过是疯狂雄蜂的叮咬……

《Krivoye Zerkalo》的下一期——第11期——将于1937年10月2日星期六出版，并从该日起定期出版。

已支付的八月和九月的订阅费将自动转至十月和十一月。那些尚未支付过去月份费用的人，希望他们在良心的谴责下，会付清欠款。

不要哭得那么伤心，亲爱的读者！我们只是分别几个月，这段时间将如流星般飞逝。我们不想剥夺你们的希望，即我们可能会在 stated 期限之前——完全突然地——恢复活动。

同时，再见，期待很快重逢！
紧紧握手！

Ed. Tiapkin-Liapkin（音译），代表
整个 Krivoe Zerkalo 兄弟会

“KRIVOYE ZERKALO”
1025/25, BUBBLING WELL RD.  Шанхай, Суббота 7 Августа 1937 г.

Дорогуша - читатель!

С глубоким прискорбіем и загробным рыданіем увѣдомляю тебя, что редакція «Кривого Зеркала» на чрезвычайном собраніи, созванном на - днях, единогласно порѣшила устроить перерыв своей бшенной дѣятельности на два мѣсяца.

К этому рѣшительному шагу вынудил нас цлый ряд трагических обстоятельств, среди коих нѣкое мѣсто занимает также и травля, поднятая против нас нѣкоторыми русскими чинами ф. п., яростными японофилами и фашистами. Но их «удары», в общем, — укусы взбѣшенных шмелей...

Слѣдующій — 11-ый номер «Кривого Зеркала» выйдет в субботу 2 октября 1937 года, и с этого числа снова будет выходить нормально.

Подписная плата, внесенная вперед за август и сентябрь мѣсяцы будет автоматически переключена на октябрь и ноябрь. Не уплатившіе за прошедшіе мѣсяцы, надо надѣяться, мучимые совѣстью, уплатят должное.

Не плачь так горько, дорогой читатель! Разстаемся всего только на пару мѣсяцев, которые промелькнут, как метеоры. Не лишаем тебя надежды, что можем возобновить нашу дѣятельность и ранѣе поставленнаго срока — совершенно внезапно.

А за сим — до скораго свиданья! Жмем крѣпко твою лапу.

ТЯПКИН - ЛЯПКИН,
Упал - намоченный всей
кривозеркальной братіи.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
No. S. B. D. 8018
Date 6 - 8 - 37
Deputy Commissioner in Charge.

I forward herewith translation of French Police
report dated July 20, 1937, on the subject of the Russian
magazine "Krivoe Zerkalo" (The Crooked Mirror) and its
editor and publisher, Mr. N. Svetloff. Since the
offices of this magazine were removed to the Settlement
(House No. 25, Hwa Kee Avenue, 1025 Bubbling Well Road),
it has published an article criticising the French Police
for the action taken against him. In view of Svetloff's
past activities and unfavourable record in the French
Concession, and the fact that he is still inclined to
publish undesirable matter using the International
Settlement as a refuge, I would suggest that he be called
to Police Headquarters and warned against continuing his
present policy of publishing libellous articles against
the local authorities or prominent members of the Russian
community.

J.B.R.

"Krivoe Zerkalo" (Crooked Mirror), No.10, July 31, 1937.
(Editor & publisher : N. Svetloff. Office : House 25,
Hwa Kee Avenue, Bubbling Well Road)

SHANGHAI, July 31.

Today's issue, so to speak, in a certain sense, is
somehow a jubilee number. It is "the tenth" issue, nevertheless.
Ten issues in the life of the "Crooked Mirror" is a
great epoch, full of everyday alarms, heartbreakings and a
helpless struggle.
Any other editor would have sat down a little and
grieved, but I, thank God, am still walking around and have
not even gone crooked.
On account of such a solemn event - i.e. our
jubilee - the "Abyssinian police" arranged a benefit for us
here. - Such a noisy benefit! don't you know.
The gay comedy - "Roll out of our concession on
a sausage"
The principal actors who took part in this comedy
were the employees of the —— Police, Messrs Rossinzon
and Apreilevitch, who, with particularly great success,
played that part of the piece where both of them, to
outshine the other, wrote lengthy and complaining reports
about the editor of the "Crooked Mirror". The affair was
very effective where the editor of the above mentioned
newspaper rode astride both these tell-tales whipping them
from behind.
The public laughed itself hoarse.
It is said that the benefit has not finished yet
and that the group of actors will present more new comedies.
We are living, generally, by the enlightened
covenants of Stalin.
Life has become better - life has become gayer!
Although in reality, perhaps, it can be that life,
so to speak, will thrash us at the tail end man.

《Krivoe Zerkalo》（歪曲的镜子）的报纸文章译文，1937年7月31日第10期。
（编辑及出版商：N. Svetloff。办公室：静安寺路华琪路25号）

上海，7月31日。

今天的这期，可以说，在某种意义上，有点像是纪念特刊。毕竟是“第十”期，无论如何。
对于《歪曲的镜子》的生命历程来说，十期是一个伟大的时代，充满了日常的惊恐、心碎和无助的斗争。
任何其他编辑都会坐下来稍作哀悼，但我，感谢上帝，还在四处走动，甚至没有变得扭曲。
由于这样一个庄严的事件——即我们的周年纪念——“阿比西尼亚警察”在这里为我们举办了一场义演。——你知道，多么喧闹的义演！
欢快的喜剧——“像香肠一样滚出我们的租界”
参与这部喜剧的主要演员是 —— 警察局的雇员，Rossinzon（音译）先生和 Apreilevitch（音译）先生，他们特别成功地演绎了剧中两人争相写长篇抱怨报告指控《歪曲的镜子》编辑的那一部分。高潮部分非常有效，上述报纸的编辑骑在这两个告密者身上，从后面鞭打他们。
公众笑得嗓子都哑了。
据说义演尚未结束，这群演员还将呈现更多新的喜剧。
总的来说，我们生活在斯大林的光辉遗训之下。
生活变得更好了——生活变得更快乐了！
虽然实际上，也许，生活，可以说，会把我们打得落花流水。

（批：存档 / J.B.R. / 8月4日）
（批：X / 法国人？）
（印：M3 / 1937年8月3日 / 上海）
（批：el. / 副本已发送给 Sanky 先生 / J.B.R. 8月3日。）

"Krivoe Zerkalo"(Crooked Mirror).
№ 10. July 31, 1937.

Шанхай. 31 іюля.
Сегодняшній номер, так сказать, въ нѣкотором родѣ какъ-бы юбилейный. Все таки десятый номер, как ни как.
В жизни „Кривого Зеркала“ десять номеров - это огромная эпоха, полная каждодневных тревог, волненій и безконечной борьбы. За эти десять номеров другой редактор посѣдѣл бы и сгорбился а я, слава Богу, еще бодренько шагаю, и даже не окривѣлъ.
По такому торжественному случаю нашему юбилею - абиссинская полиція нам бенефис здѣсь устроила. Такой, знаете, шумный бенефис!
Была поставлена веселая комедія «Катись колбаской съ нашей концессіи».
Главными дѣйствующими лицами выступали въ этой комедіи служащіе полиціи г. Россинзон и г. Апрѣлевич, которые съ особенно большим успѣхом исполняли то мѣсто въ пьес, гдѣ они оба наперегонку писали на редактора газеты „Окосѣвшее Зеркало“ длинные и жалобные доносы. Очень эффектным был апофеоз, гдѣ редактор упомянутой газеты ѣздил на обоих доносчиках верхом, погоняя их сзади прутом. Публика гоготала до колики.
Говорят, что этим бенефис не кончится и что труппа комедіантов затѣвает новыя веселыя постановки.
Мы, вообще, живем по по свѣтлым завѣтам Сталина:
— Жить стало лучше, жить стало веселѣе!
Хотя на самом дѣлѣ, может быть, и жизнь нас, так сказать, и в хвост и въ гриву колотит.
Пушай се там развлекается. А мы по теоріи Эйнштейна жарим:
— Все, дескать, относительно!
Сегодня ты, а завтра я, а въ том же духѣ обра...
ТЯПКИН ЛЯПКИН Т

Date July 26, 1937.
Subject "Krivoye Zerkalo", Russian weekly publication.
Made by D.S. Iroshnikov Forwarded by C. Crawford. S.I.

With reference to the attached letter dated July 21,
1937, from Mr. N. Svetloff, editor and publisher of the
"Krivoye Zerkalo" (Crooked Mirror) - a "weekly organ of free
humour", I have to state that this publication made its first
appearance on May 29, 1937 and that until July 10 its editor-
ial office was located at 506 Route Vallon.
From the first issues of the "Krivoye Zerkalo" it
became apparent that scandal-mongering was its main feature.
Singling out certain individuals and organizations as targets
of his vulgar, insinuative and often libellous remarks is
another speciality of Mr. Svetloff.
It is reported that the editor was several times
called up to the French Police Headquarters in connection
with letters of complaint against him received by the Police
as well as in connection with certain articles containing
remarks derogatory to the Japanese. On July 19 he was
fined $40 (or 20 days detention) by the 2nd Shanghai
Special District Court for publishing a libellous statement
concerning Mr. Ch. E. Metzler, Chairman of the Russian
Emigrants' Committee.
Feeling that the Authorities of the French Concession
did not favour his literary activities Svetloff removed the
editorial office of his publication first to House 5, Yang
Terrace, Weihaiwei Road, and later to House 20, Hwa Kee
Avenue, Bubbling Well Road.

关于附件中日期为1937年7月21日的 N. Svetloff 先生的来信，他是《Krivoye Zerkalo》（歪曲的镜子）——一份“自由幽默周刊”的编辑和出版商，我必须陈述，该出版物首次出现于1937年5月29日，直到7月10日，其编辑部位于瓦隆路506号。

TRANSLATION

David and Goliath
A satire by a member of the "Satiricon"

They were placed side by side. The examination
commenced. The adversaries did not move. They were
listening to the Judge's words:

"Your turn" says the latter addressing himself to
"David", tell all you have to say in order to rehabilitate
yourself.

"What can I say, Your Honour, asks David? it is
no longer possible to exist on account of all these
"representatives". Especially as it is difficult to know
which are legal representatives and which are not.

"Do not deviate from the question, cuts in the Judge,
do you admit your guilt?"

"If he wants to understand, says "David" pointing to
"Goliath" with the movement of his head, the expression
"dirty hands" as a trivial expression meaning thief, that
is is his business. But we have, Your Honour, another
literary expression in the Russian language, namely: "The cap
burns on a thief's head". (A guilty mind is never at ease). (1)

"Why are you silent, whispers Goliath's lawyer
giving him a push, go on defend yourself, confound it,
defend your honour. Don't you see that he is making a
new hint ....

"Whisper to him what he has to say, add Goliath's
adherents in low tones, it is so hot that his brain is a
little out of order".

"It is for you to speak" says the Judge to "Goliath".

(1) Russian proverb which means that sooner or later a
person who has committed an offence will betray himself.

译文

大卫与歌利亚
“讽刺家”（Satiricon）成员所作的讽刺作品

他们并排而坐。审讯
开始。对手们一动不动。他们在
聆听法官的话语：

“轮到你了”，后者对
“大卫”说道，说出你需要说的一切以恢复你的名誉。

“我能说什么呢，法官大人？”大卫问道？由于所有这些
“代表”，已经无法生存了。尤其是很难知道
哪些是合法代表，哪些不是。

“不要偏离问题”，法官打断道，“你承认有罪吗？”

“如果他想理解的话，”“大卫”指着
“歌利亚”点头说道，“‘脏手’这一表达作为意指小偷的通俗说法，那是
他的事。但是，法官大人，我们在俄语中有另一个文学表达，即：‘帽子在小偷头上燃烧’。”（做贼心虚）。(1)

“你为什么沉默？”歌利亚的律师低声说道，
推了他一下，“继续辩护，该死的，捍卫你的荣誉。你没看到他在做出
新的暗示吗....

“低声告诉他该说什么，”歌利亚的追随者
轻声补充道，“天气太热，他的脑子有点乱了”。

“由你发言”，法官对“歌利亚”说。

(1) 俄罗斯谚语，意为犯罪的人迟早会自我暴露。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

This latter opens his mouth several times convulsively,
like a pike drawn out of water, and utters inarticulate
sounds .....

"Speak louder, orders the Judge.

"Vou-bou-bou, groans Goliath, I want to say that ...
He has insulted me, the good-for-nothing wretch. He has
covered with shame my grey Aryan head .... (I)

"Express yourself more definitely, requests the Judge.
An awkward silence follows.

David leans with an expression of kind concern towards
his mortal enemy and whispers to him what he should say ....

Overcoming his shame and confusion, Goliath listens
to David's words ......

"I accuse, shouts Goliath all of a sudden in a fierce
manner. To prison with the vagabond! Whip him a hundred
times and pull his nostrils out. Shoot him ..."

David's adherents sob. My God, he gave so much
hope. He composed verses ... In other words he was a poet.

"I never liked writers, says a little woman, maintaining
a neutral attitude. It is a very suspicious profession.
To-day it is poetry and to-morrow prison. All writers are
convicts."

"Have courage, whispers someone to David. Do not lose
your face. Be worthy of the best traditions of the Russian
literature. Of course, it is naturally different where
prison is concerned, it will be difficult for you to compete
with DOSTOEVSKY ....

(1) An expression impossible to translate exactly. It may
be understood in a much worse sense i.e. "Covered with
filth and sweepings".
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

后者几次痉挛般地张开嘴，
像一条被拖出水面的梭子鱼，发出含糊不清的声音.....

“大声点”，法官命令道。

“呜-布-布”，歌利亚呻吟道，“我想说... 他侮辱了我，这个无赖。他让我的
灰白雅利安头颅蒙羞.... (I)

“表达得更明确些”，法官要求道。随之而来的是尴尬的沉默。

大卫带着一种善意的关切表情倾向他的死敌，低声告诉他该说什么....

克服羞愧和困惑，歌利亚听着
大卫的话......

“我指控，”歌利亚突然猛烈地喊道，“把这个流浪汉关进监狱！鞭打他一百下，拔掉他的鼻孔。枪毙他...”

大卫的追随者在抽泣。天哪，他给了那么多
希望。他创作诗歌... 换句话说，他是个诗人。

“我从不喜欢作家，”一个小女人说，保持中立态度。“这是一个非常可疑的职业。今天是诗歌，明天是监狱。所有作家都是罪犯。”

“要有勇气，”有人对大卫低语。“不要丢脸。要配得上俄国
文学的最佳传统。当然，在监狱方面自然不同，你很难与陀思妥耶夫斯基（DOSTOEVSKY）竞争....

M.E. MOROSOW

153C Route des Soeurs, Apt. 7. Shanghai, July 2, 1937.

Chief of French Police, Shanghai.

Sir,

In accordance with instructions given me by Mr.
C.E. METZLER, Chairman of the Russian Emigrants' Committee
in Shanghai, I have the honour to request you to give me
your assistance in regard to the following:

In issue No. 5 dated June 26 of the "Crooked Mirror"
published and distributed in the French Concession, the
following lines appear regarding my client:

"METZLER.

Heart hunter and hard man of the world.

(Jal na roukou ne tchist) - soiled hands as a
result of dishonest actions - this expression is
equivalent to libel.

He's a true diplomat up to his nose.
(But, unfortunately, not eloquent).

The second line of the epigram constitutes a
gross offence against my client's honour, for the expression
"Na roukou ne tchist" means in Russian that he is a thief.

Taking into consideration that this seditious
attack was made against a person who occupies an irreproachable
post and also in view of the fact that having been elected
by the majority of Russian Emigrant organisations, Mr. Metzler
now occupies the position of Representative of the Emigrant
Community in Shanghai, I have to request you to give
instructions, in accordance with Article 310 (Sections 1 & 2)
and Art. 314 of the Criminal Code, as well as Arts. 19 & 35
of the Press Law, for the guilty parties - editor, printer
and author of the above mentioned paper, to be prosecuted
according to law.

Attached please find one copy of the paper in question.

Yours, etc.

MOROSOW.

M.E. MOROSOW

上海，霞飞路（Route des Soeurs）153C号7室。1937年7月2日。

致上海法租界警务处总监。

先生：

遵照上海俄国侨民委员会主席C.E. METZLER先生给予我的指示，我谨就以下事项请求阁下予以协助：

在6月26日出版并于法租界发行的《歪镜报》（Crooked Mirror）第5期中，出现了有关我方委托人的如下文字：

“METZLER。

猎心者，世故冷酷之人。

‘Jal na roukou ne tchist’——因不诚实行为而双手肮脏——此表述等同于诽谤。

他是一个彻头彻尾的外交家。
（但不幸的是，并不善辩）。

这首讽刺诗的第二行严重冒犯了我方委托人的名誉，因为俄语表达‘Na roukou ne tchist’意指他是小偷。

考虑到此次煽动性攻击针对的是一位身居无可指摘职位的人士，同时也鉴于Metzler先生经大多数俄国侨民组织选举，目前担任上海侨民社区代表一职，我恳请阁下依据《刑法典》第310条（第1及2款）和第314条，以及《新闻法》第19条和第35条，下达指令，依法起诉上述报刊的责任人——即编辑、印刷商和作者。

随函附上该报刊一份。

此致，

MOROSOW。

E.N. SHENDRIKOFF
BARRISTER AT LAW
Shanghai, 29th June 1937.
304, Rue Cardinal Mercier

Directeur des Service de Police,
Shanghai.

Sir;

In published in French Concession a mosquito newspaper
"False Mirror" in No.4 et 5, there were admitted, as with
regards to me, as to my wife Mrs. K.V. Shendrikoff, absolutely
improbable things, which blame a good name, by mocking.
Particularly there is seditious article placed in No.5
of 26th June under the name: "Mrs Shendrikoff is invited in
Moscow." Not entering into consideration of contents of said
article, it is quite sufficiently to draw attention in its
beginning, which brings an imputation upon my wife's character,
suggesting to readers improbable hypothesises, which blame her
good name.
For your information, I beg to advise you, that a few
days before appearance of said newspaper, editor of same
Tiapkin-Liapkin, he is also N.F. Svetloff, and by facts Mr.
N. Svinin has come in my office requesting my subscription and
advertisement. I gave him one dollar, as subscription's
charge but absolutely refused to give him any advertisement.
In No.1 of said newspaper there was no my advertisement but
in No.2, I was very much surprised to see the same. In this
respect I have sent a letter to editors of Russian newspapers
"Shanghai Zaria" and "Slovo" in which I categorically objected
against placing my advertisement in such kind of press.
After that, in No.3, there was placed an article, under
the heading "Eliah the God of Thunder", which ascribed to me
wrong facts, with indication that said article is placed only
because I have protested against publishing my advertisement
in their newspaper.
.In No.4 of the same newspaper, there was published the
article, as I said above, with regards to my wife and in
separate paragraph about myself too.
I should not apply to you with this request, it my wife
would be here and did not go for summer holidays from Shanghai.
Besides, those pasquinades have such a form that publishing an
improbable things, they do not give a sufficient reasons for
calling editor before a judge in criminal court for blaming.
I absolutely not sure, that in next issues there will
be again a same pasquinades against my near relations who are
absent from Shanghai at present and therefore, I apply to you
with respectful request to use your authority over the said
Tiapkins-Liapkins who are using the permission of French
authorities for edition of mosquito newspaper with purpose to
blame with impunity the good names of people.
Thanking you in anticipation for your kind attention
to my letter, I beg to remain,

Sir,
Yours very truly,

(Sd.) E.N. Shendrikoff.

E.N. SHENDRIKOFF
律师
上海，1937年6月29日。
麦神父路（Rue Cardinal Mercier）304号

致上海警务处处长。

先生：

在法租界出版的小报《歪镜报》（False Mirror）第4期和第5期中，刊登了关于我及我妻子K.V. Shendrikoff女士的绝对荒谬之事，通过嘲讽损害了好名声。特别是6月26日第5期中有一篇题为《Shendrikoff夫人受邀前往莫斯科》的煽动性文章。无需深入探讨该文内容，仅其开头部分就足以引起注意，因为它对我妻子的品格进行了指责，向读者暗示荒谬的假设，从而损害她的名誉。

供阁下参考，特此告知，在该报出版前几天，其编辑Tiapkin-Liapkin（即N.F. Svetloff，事实上是N. Svinin先生）曾来到我的办公室，要求我订阅并刊登广告。我付给他一美元作为订阅费，但断然拒绝刊登任何广告。在该报第1期中没有我的广告，但在第2期中，我很惊讶地看到了它。就此，我曾致信俄文报纸《上海朝霞报》（Shanghai Zaria）和《言论报》（Slovo）的编辑，明确反对在此类报刊上刊登我的广告。

此后，在第3期中，刊登了一篇题为《雷神伊利亚》的文章，将不实事实归咎于我，并指出刊登该文仅仅是因为我抗议在他们报纸上刊登我的广告。

正如我上面所说，在同一份报纸的第4期中，刊登了关于我妻子的文章，并在单独一段中也提及了我本人。

如果我妻子在此且未离开上海去度暑假，我就不会提出此请求。此外，这些讽刺文章的形式虽然刊登了荒谬之事，但不足以提供充分理由在刑事法庭以诽谤罪起诉编辑。

我完全不能确定，在下一期中是否会出现针对我目前不在上海的近亲的类似讽刺文章，因此，我恭敬地请求阁下运用您对上述Tiapkins-Liapkins的权威，他们利用法国当局的许可出版小报，目的是肆无忌惮地损害人们的名誉。

预先感谢您对我信函的关注，

先生，
您忠实的，

（签名）E.N. Shendrikoff。

682 Avenue Joffre, Apt. 3        Shanghai, July 6, 1937.

Chief of French Police, Shanghai.

STATEMENT

Mr. N.F. SVETLOFF, editor of the "Crooked Mirror"
magazine, 506 Route Vallon, has demanded that I advertise

desire, he commenced publishing in his paper of June 12,

KRIVOE ZERKALO
----
Shanghai, July 5, 1937.

"Le Mirror deformant"
journal humoristic russe.

To the Director of French Police

Dear Sir,
    In connection with several complaints of some
residents of Shanghai who intimated that I allegedly offended
them in my paper, I have repeatedly been called to the
political department of French Police.
    I have explained already that all these complaints
are not based on facts, while all what was written in my
paper was confirmed by facts and documents which I can furnish
if necessary.
    As a matter of fact I have to warn you that this
current of complaints is caused by purely political news of
some reactionary and fascist-inclined people who are
dissatisfied with my newspaper which is democratic in
character.
    I am very surprised that these people who allege
that I offended them do not resort to legal means of
prosecution. If they fined that I have acted against existing
laws they should furnish their complaints to the court where
I am ready to answer any accusation.
    Concerning Mr. Kedrolivansky who is offended that
I described him as "Mercenary Man" I must state that I have
meant only his criminal work against Russia in collaboration
with Japanese Police. He has not disclaimed that statement of
mine and obviously cannot disclaim.
    I hope that you will keep in your mind all the
abovesaid and will not surprise me but, on the contrary, will
aid me and my paper, for my only aim is to prevent harmful
activity of some Russian people against the interest of
Russia, I believe that these people are as averse to you as
they are to me.
    I wonder if free press cannot exist here, in the
French Concession, which is the part of Belle France where
freedom of word is unlimited.
    I beg you again to keep in mind all the abovesaid
and give your order to analyze the unduly complaints against
me before calling me to the police, because it takes too much
precious time and greatly disturbs me.

Respectfully yours,

"Editor of 'Krivoe Zerkalo'"

Sd. N. Svetloff

P.S. Concerning some Ukrainian who are dissatisfied with
my newspaper, they also cannot disclaim that they
are working in collaboration with German Consulate.

上海，1937年7月5日。

“Le Mirror deformant”
俄文幽默期刊。

致法租界警务处处长

亲爱的先生：

由于一些上海居民投诉称我在报纸中冒犯了他们，我已多次被传唤至法租界警务处政治部。

我已经解释过，所有这些投诉都缺乏事实依据，而我报纸上所写的一切均有事实和文件证实，如有需要我可以提供。

事实上，我必须警告阁下，这股投诉潮纯粹是由一些反动和倾向法西斯主义的人引起的，他们对我的具有民主性质的报纸感到不满。

我很惊讶，这些声称被我冒犯的人不诉诸法律手段进行起诉。如果他们发现我违反了现行法律，他们应向法庭提交投诉，我准备回应任何指控。

关于Kedrolivansky先生，他因我将他描述为“雇佣兵式人物”而感到被冒犯，我必须声明，我所指的仅是他与日本警察合作从事的反俄犯罪活动。他并未否认我的这一说法，显然也无法否认。

我希望阁下能记住上述所有情况，不要让我感到意外，相反，希望能援助我和我的报纸，因为我唯一的目标是防止一些俄国人从事损害俄罗斯利益的活动，我相信这些人既厌恶我也厌恶阁下。

我不禁要问，在这座美丽法兰西的一部分、言论自由无限的法租界，难道不能存在新闻自由吗？

我再次恳请阁下记住上述所有情况，并在传唤我到警局之前，下令对针对我的不当投诉进行分析，因为这耗费了太多宝贵时间，并极大地干扰了我。

此致，

“《Krivoe Zerkalo》编辑”

签名 N. Svetloff

附言：关于一些对我的报纸不满的乌克兰人，他们也无法否认他们正在与德国领事馆合作。
